findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile parent AC4/AC1 with child 3f27's sanctioned retention of `_mutation_to_batch_dict` and the polymorphic `apply()` selection — either amend the parent AC to name these as explicit justified public carve-outs, or delete them per the AC.
evidence: Parent AC4: '`_mutation_to_batch_dict`, polymorphic legacy `apply` selection, duplicate CREATE shapes, and obsolete compatibility dispatch/re-exports are deleted in this epic; one production route remains.'
3f27 AC evidence: 'the function is retained as the now-unambiguous typed→dict adapter `apply()`'s legacy `list[dict]` calling convention still needs.'
3f27 AC evidence: "`applier.apply()`'s `isinstance(m, MutationShape)` ternary (target (b)) is KEPT: deleting it broke ~50 tests ... Sanctioned justified carve-out."
Parent AC1 also requires consumers to 'consume it without generic action payload dictionaries', yet the retained `_mutation_to_batch_dict` still produces dicts on the production route.
findings.finding: Parent AC4 requires `_mutation_to_batch_dict` and 'polymorphic legacy `apply` selection' to be DELETED in this epic, but child 3f27 (the sole owner of AC4) explicitly RETAINS both: it keeps `_mutation_to_batch_dict` as a 'now-unambiguous typed→dict adapter' and keeps `applier.apply()`'s `isinstance(m, MutationShape)` ternary as a 'sanctioned justified carve-out'. This is a bypass-annotation contradiction — the parent AC says delete, the child annotates a retention exception — so the epic is structurally guaranteed to fail the parent AC4 completion check as written.
scenarios: Epic completion verifier evaluates parent AC4 against the landed tree: `_mutation_to_batch_dict` and the polymorphic `apply()` selection still exist, so the AC is not satisfied as written.
A reader of parent AC1 expects zero generic action-payload dicts on the production route; the typed→dict adapter re-introduces one.
findings.suggested_fix: Amend parent AC4 to read that `_mutation_to_batch_dict` and the `apply(list[dict])` selection MAY be retained only as an explicitly-public, census-justified adapter (naming the second calling convention they serve), and reword AC1's 'without generic action payload dictionaries' to scope to the typed producer boundary rather than the terminal adapter.

evidence: Parent AC11: 'Final epic evidence reports deleted representations/routes/ambient authorities and demonstrates that no cleanup item was deferred solely to keep both old and new paths live.'
3f27 scope is reconciler-only ('typed production route and removal of compatibility dispatch'); its evidence covers `_mutation_to_batch_dict`/apply but not config/LLM ambient authorities.
3a08 evidence covers only CLI/command/store shadow deletion; ec44 covers only LLM + remaining non-LLM shadow deletion.
No roster AC aggregates deleted reconciler routes AND deleted ambient config/LLM authorities into one final report, nor asserts the 'nothing deferred to keep both paths live' invariant epic-wide.
findings.finding: Parent AC11 requires a 'Final epic evidence report [that] reports deleted representations/routes/ambient authorities and demonstrates that no cleanup item was deferred solely to keep both old and new paths live.' No sibling in the roster owns this consolidated epic-final synthesis: 3f27 reports only the reconciler-route deletions, 3a08/ec44 report only their own config-shadow deletions, and each is scoped to its own story. The absence test holds across the whole roster — no indexed AC delivers the cross-cutting 'no cleanup deferred to keep both paths live' demonstration spanning reconciler + CLI/command/store + LLM.
scenarios: Epic close: the completion verifier looks for a single evidence artifact enumerating every deleted representation/route/ambient authority and attesting no dual-path deferral; it finds only per-story fragments.
This AC is directly undercut by the AC4 retention finding — items WERE kept, so the 'nothing deferred to keep both paths live' claim needs explicit epic-level justification that no child produces.
findings.suggested_fix: Add the AC11 final-evidence deliverable to the last-landing child (3f27 or ec44, whichever closes last) or create a dedicated epic-close ticket that aggregates the deletion censuses from 3f27/3a08/ec44 and explicitly reconciles the sanctioned `_mutation_to_batch_dict`/`apply()` retentions against the 'no dual-path deferral' bar.
